newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FTC repeals used oil labeling rule.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FTC repeals used oil labeling rule.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Trade Commission Thursday said it has repealed its Used Oil Rule because it has been pre-empted by the Recycled Oil Rule which the agency issued a year ago.

The FTC said the Used Oil Rule's labeling and advertising requirements for engine oils were overtaken by the Recycled Oil Rule, which the agency issued as part of the Energy Policy and Conservation Act. The recycled rule allows manufacturers and sellers to represent that recycled oil is substantially equivalent to new engine oil, as long as that is determined by test procedures prescribed by the FTC.
The FTC said it only received three comments on the issue, and all supported repeal.

"After reviewing the rulemaking record, and in light of the Recycled Oil Rule, the Commission has determined that the Used Oil Rule no longer is necessary and that its repeal will avoid any inconsistency with EPCA's goals," the FTC statement said.
